display.clozeStimulus: The fibers of the infraspinatus muscle attach the scapula to the humerus and rotate the arm __________.
The latissimus dorsi rotates the humerus __________ and adducts the arm from a raised position.
The __________ that move the thigh are attached to the femur and to part of the pelvic girdle.
The teres minor is a small muscle connecting the __________ to the humerus.
The humerus extends the __________ and can also adduct and rotate the arm medially.
The femur flexes the hip and adducts the __________.
The supraspinatus connects the scapula to the greater __________ of the humerus and abducts the arm.
The ulna flexes the __________ and adducts the hand.
Sodium ions diffuse inward through the open sodium channels, down their concentration gradient, aided by the __________ of the sodium ions to the negative charges on the inside of the membrane.
The myelin sheath would prevent the __________ of an impulse, if the sheath were continuous along the length of the axon.
The general pattern is that neurons receive input through the __________ and the cell body, and send output in the form of an impulse conducted away from the cell body, down the axon.
If an axon of a neuron within the CNS is separated from its cell body, the __________ __________ of the axon will degenerate, but more slowly than a separated axon in the PNS.
If the __________ becomes less negative than the resting potential, the __________ is depolarized.
A network of fine threads called __________ extends into the axon and support it.
__________ are found throughout the nervous system, and in the brain they greatly outnumber neurons.
__________ can be classified by functional differences into the following groups, depending on whether they carry information into the CNS, completely within the CNS, or out of the CNS.
The increased calcium concentration inside the cell initiates a series of events that fuses the synaptic vesicles with the cell membrane, where they release their __________ by exocytosis.
Myelin gives the cell membranes of Schwann cells a higher __________ of lipid than other cell membranes.
The nodes of __________ between Schwann cells or oligodendrocytes interrupt the myelin sheath.
Neurons are excitable; that is, they can respond to changes in their __________.
Pathways connect the __________ to the cerebral cortex, thalamus, and parts of the brainstem so that it can receive impulses from them and send impulses to them.
__________ on all reflexes enter the CNS and constitute a sensory or afferent limb of the reflex.
Meningitis, an __________ of the meninges usually caused by bacterial or viral infection of the CSF, affects the arachnoid and pia maters and sometimes the dura mater, mostly in children.
A mass of white matter that makes up the bulk of the cerebrum contains bundles of __________ axons that connect neuron cell bodies of the cortex with other parts of the nervous system.
The spinal cord __________ where nervous tissue leaves the cranial cavity at the level of the foramen magnum.
Striking the patellar ligament just below the patella initiates the patellar __________.
The cerebral cortex covers the gyri, dipping into the __________ and fissures.
The basal nuclei are often called the basal ganglia, but __________ a ganglion is a cluster of neuron cell bodies in the peripheral nervous system.
Five cavities persist in the mature brain as the fluid- filled __________ and the tubes that connect them.
In 1953, a surgeon removed parts of the __________ and the amygdala of a young man to relieve his severe epilepsy.
The lobes of each __________ include the following: All lobes of the cerebrum have a thin layer of gray matter called the cerebral cortex.
When the rectus abdominis muscle contracts, it tenses the abdominal wall and compresses the contents of the __________ __________.
The deltoid is a thick, __________ __________ that covers the shoulder joint.
The middle trapezius fibers pull the scapula toward the __________ __________, and the lower fibers draw the scapula and shoulder downward.

The __________ __________ also ensures that an action potential is conducted in only one direction, down the axon, because the area upstream from where the action potential has just occurred is still in the __________ __________ from the previous action potential.
An action potential causes a __________ __________ to flow away from the trigger zone through the cytoplasm of the axon.
The axon or a group of axons may lie partially or completely in a __________ __________ of a Schwann cell.
An important part of the __________ __________ at the cellular level is not a cell at all, but the functional connection between a neuron and the cell with which it communicates, called a synapse.
If the __________ __________ becomes more negative than the resting potential, the membrane is hyperpolarized.
The thalamus is a __________ __________ for sensory impulses ascending from other parts of the nervous system to the cerebral cortex.
The thalamus receives all __________ __________ and channels them to appropriate regions of the cortex for interpretation.
The spinal cord is a center for __________ __________, and it is a conduit for impulses to and from the brain.
The quadriceps femoris muscle group, attached to the patella by a tendon, is pulled slightly, stimulating __________ __________ in the muscle group.
An area of the __________ __________, the amygdala, assigns value to a memory, such as whether it was pleasant.
The hypothalamus lies inferior to the thalamic nuclei and forms the lower walls and floor of the __________ __________.
The brain lies in the cranial cavity of the skull, and the spinal cord occupies the __________ __________ in the vertebral column.

A __________ __________ of the reticular formation frees the cortex from what would otherwise be a continual bombardment of sensory stimulation and allows it to concentrate on more significant information.
The pectoralis minor runs laterally and upward from the ribs to the scapula and pulls the scapula __________ __________ __________.
The __________ __________ that are associated with the spinal cord have cell bodies that are not in the spinal cord at all.

The __________ __________ of the ganglia provides the autonomic nervous system with some degree of independence from the brain and spinal cord, and the visceral efferent nerve fibers associated with these ganglia comprise the autonomic nervous system.
